records.locator: Adhyaya III opening editorial note, physical PDF494 / printed96
records.source_paraphrase: Sastri states that 46 of the 80 slokas in Jātaka's third chapter are taken from Bṛhat Jātaka; he lists the individual ranges.
records.caveat: Reported source lineage, not independently collated Sanskrit or evidence of 46 forecasts.

records.locator: Adhyaya III introduction and verse1, PDF494–495 / printed96–97
records.source_paraphrase: The source gives Moon's dvādaśāṃśa with malefic/benefic strength and angular conditions in proposed animal/plant birth predictions; Sastri explicitly notes that amśa here is D12 rather than ordinary D9.
records.caveat: Do not silently code Navāṃśa/D9; the extension to lost animals/cultivation is an editor's stated application and requires extra horary input.

records.locator: Adhyaya III verse66, PDF550 / printed162
records.source_paraphrase: Stronger of Lagna sign versus rising Navāṃśa is said to distinguish birth at paternal home, at distant building, in outbuilding or at maternal grandfather's house under vargottama.
records.caveat: Family birth setting must be documented and time uncertain; note close alternative conditions instead of choosing favorable site.

records.locator: Adhyaya IV opening editor note, PDF571 / printed173
records.source_paraphrase: Sastri identifies IV.17–18, IV.32–39 and IV.99 as taken from Bṛhat Jātaka.
records.caveat: Textual borrowing claims require independent author/edition verification; not independent evidence of infant prediction.

records.locator: Adhyaya IV verse1, PDF571 / printed173
records.source_paraphrase: The source states lifespan cannot be determined reliably in the first twelve years, even while the chapter lists claimed childhood-death rules.
records.caveat: Historical/source-internal self-limitation; no personal child-health or mortality forecasting.

records.locator: Adhyaya IV verse17, PDF578–579 / printed180–181
records.source_paraphrase: The text assigns planetary rulers to successive gestational months and proposes outcomes from their dignity, introducing an additional conception-time chart and medical-development assumptions.
records.caveat: Historical embryology is not modern medical fact. Miscarriage/birth prediction is not actionable health guidance.

records.locator: Adhyaya V opening and verse1, PDF631 / printed233
records.source_paraphrase: Jātaka explicitly lists eight named ways of calculating lifespan, including Naisargika, Pinda, Amśa, Chakra, Nakshatra, Dāya and Ashtakavarga variants.
records.caveat: Multiple non-equivalent calculation branches; no universally applicable answer or valid medical lifespan estimation.

records.locator: Adhyaya V verse2, PDF631 / printed233
records.source_paraphrase: The source assigns seven fixed natural periods 20, 1, 2, 9, 18, 20 and 50 years to Sun through Saturn, summing to 120 years.
records.caveat: Numeric recipe is a source assertion and not human lifespan evidence; astronomical start point and subtraction phases require further source reading.

records.locator: Adhyaya V opening editor note, PDF631 / printed233
records.source_paraphrase: Sastri singles out Adhyaya V verses 7,9,11 and 17–21 as taken from Bṛhat Jātaka.
records.caveat: Don't count two copies of a transmitted algorithm as two independent predictive validations.

records.locator: Adhyaya VI opening and verse1, PDF61 / printed319
records.source_paraphrase: The source names four categories that undermine royal-status yogas: Bhañga, Reka (poverty), Preṣya (dependence/service) and Kemadruma.
records.caveat: Opposing antecedents must be included with royal yogas before testing; socially prejudicial interpretations cannot be asserted about named people.

records.locator: Adhyaya VI editor introduction, PDF61 / printed319
records.source_paraphrase: Sastri identifies verses 48,49,50,52,99,100 as taken from Bṛhat Jātaka.
records.caveat: Historical text dependence, not independently successful observed cases.

records.locator: Adhyaya VII verse1 and subsequent NOTES, PDF114 / printed372
records.source_paraphrase: The author lists extreme sign-arrangement political fortunes; Sastri's NOTES say the author condensed named yogas and attach additional verses from other treatises to expand it.
records.caveat: Only the original verse's exact planet/sign configuration belongs to Vaidyanātha without further attribution; physical feasibility not yet checked.

records.locator: Adhyaya VII verses137–138, PDF200 / printed468
records.source_paraphrase: Chāmara Yoga is said to indicate either a respected learned philosopher or a king with sacred learning; the next Saṅkha Yoga gets a different two-configuration definition.
records.caveat: Alternative statuses are not independent accurate predictions; political opportunity and 'or' logic lower specificity.

records.locator: Adhyaya VIII verse9, PDF245 / printed603
records.source_paraphrase: Several three-classical-planet conjunction sets are assigned distinct family, learned, royal, temperamental and bodily results.
records.caveat: Planet set must be unique and physically feasible; multiple broadly related consequences not separate independent witnesses.

records.locator: Adhyaya VIII around verses11–13, PDF248 / printed606
records.source_paraphrase: A three-planet combination is associated with devotion to music, poetry and drama, while different triplets are described in contrasting social/physical terms.
records.caveat: Avoid moralized, disability-related and status stereotypes as present-day personality assessments.

records.locator: Adhyaya VIII verse115, PDF323 / printed681
records.source_paraphrase: Original verse equates source-predicted magnitude in exalted, own Navāṃśa, mūlatrikoṇa, friendly Navāṃśa and adverse conditions, with an additional Sastri note citing another reading.
records.caveat: Do not apply one unqualified conjunction-outcome list to all D9 conditions or silently select alternate variant.

records.locator: Adhyaya IX verse1, PDF325 / printed583
records.source_paraphrase: The author says he will assess Gulika plus year, month, weekday and birth hour, introducing multiple astronomical/calendar inputs beyond seven natal Grahas.
records.caveat: Gulika computation must be precisely declared, lunar calendar boundaries/timezone/source version fixed.

records.locator: Adhyaya IX verse10 and related year catalog, PDF331–341 / printed589–599
records.source_paraphrase: Each of the traditional sixty-year saṃvatsara cycle receives distinct character/status predictions rather than modern Gregorian birth-year predictions.
records.caveat: Requires a historically accurate calendrical year-cycle engine and culture baseline, not human result evidence.

records.locator: Adhyaya IX verses31–39, PDF346–350 / printed604–608
records.source_paraphrase: The source assigns separate birth-month, lunar-fortnight, tithi and weekday qualities with partially overlapping consequences.
records.caveat: Same respondent answers cannot independently confirm each calendar label; multiplicity and base rates must be controlled.

records.locator: Adhyaya IX closing Sastri NOTES, PDF390 / printed648
records.source_paraphrase: After the author closes Adhyaya IX, Sastri appends verses from Kara(k)abharaṇa to time results of birth year, season, month, pakṣa, tithi and weekday via different daśā rulers.
records.caveat: The added timing algorithm is external to Vaidyanātha's original chapter, and sharing text with another book is not independent validation.

source_critical_warning: Actual physical order in uploaded combined scan places volume II early (PDF59–450) while late volume I continues PDF451–716. Printed pagination not monotonically identical to physical PDF page number.
method_prohibitions: No medical fertility or mortality advice
Do not treat Sastri editor notes as verses of Vaidyanatha
Do not count borrowed Brihat Jataka sentences as independent predictive confirmation
No natal model or questionnaire changed
